conclusion: No confirmed owner credential leak or identifiable patient records found. Publication should first remove the full upstream archive/cache payload from reachable Git history or establish its independent redistribution scope. Source contacts, public study titles and pseudonymous sample filenames are not classified as private patient identifiers.
methods: Enumerated every reachable Git object across all refs; scanned all 597 unique blobs and compared all tracked worktree files to HEAD.
Read all 760 regular tar members in memory without extracting into the repository; scanned 185,939,835 uncompressed bytes overall.

Pattern scans for private keys, AWS/GitHub/model tokens, JWTs, authenticated/signed URLs, credential assignments, user paths, RFC1918 IPs, emails, and direct patient-identifier field names; values not included in this report.

Additional generic credential-assignment pass found 136 code/template/fixture references; reviewed all 46 non-placeholder heuristic hits. Two Figshare share keys, one duplicated publisher casa_token URL and one source-published Baidu extraction password are separately flagged; no owner account secret confirmed.
Examined archive schemas, cache descriptions/license fields, sample image metadata, all five local gallery images visually, README claims, and all resource-page overview/sample headings.

findings.evidence: Archive expands to 164,507,880 bytes; hub/audit occupies 152,072,605 bytes. Candidate details contain 2,755 records (2,155 Kaggle / 319 Figshare / 281 Hugging Face), including unrelated commercial ISO-certification text, self-driving, wind-energy, and lengthy copied descriptions. The file-list field alone serializes about 45.7 MB and descriptions about 3.23 MB, with further duplicates in search JSON/CSV. Source terms include unknown=900, missing=326, other=136 and copyright-authors=27. Upstream LICENSE expressly limits its MIT grant to library code, so that notice alone does not resolve all cached third-party description/file-list permissions. This is an unresolved redistribution/scope issue, not proof of infringement.
findings.fix: Before public release, remove the full archive from every reachable public Git commit and remove its build dependency; preserve the pinned upstream URL, commit/tag and SHA256, plus the minimal required reviewed metadata and suitable attribution. A normal deletion in a new commit will not remove the original blob from public history. Alternatively establish separate permission/terms for the entire cache. Update README/archive instructions to the resulting packaging.

findings.evidence: Two literal 20-character Figshare share keys occur in upstream dataset helper constants and adjacent /s/ URLs, explicitly described there as private shares for ACRIMA and OculoScope. These appear to be pre-existing resource locators rather than this owner’s API credentials; no token values are reproduced. The audit did not verify whether each share URL is intentionally public or still authorizes a restricted preview.
findings.fix: Removing the upstream executable/cache archive removes this redundant exposure. Retain canonical publisher/record URLs in curated entries and verify any remaining share-link publication basis; do not rotate someone else’s keys or label them a confirmed account leak.

findings.evidence: The broader assignment pass found an opaque casa_token query value on a Taylor & Francis article URL copied into metadata (duplicated in JSON/CSV), plus a Baidu NetDisk extraction password inside a public-source description. Values are not reproduced or tested. These may be public sharing/access affordances or expired publisher tokens; ownership and validity are not established. They are not confirmed credentials belonging to this repository owner.
findings.fix: Remove the archive from reachable history, or strip these query credentials/access codes from any retained source snapshot and keep canonical DOI/landing links. Do not test the opaque token to establish access.

findings.evidence: Author and committer metadata contain the owner’s institutional email address (not a GitHub noreply address). This is normal Git attribution and not a secret, but a public repository will expose it regardless of file-level email cleanup. Address omitted from this report.
findings.fix: No change required if public institutional attribution is intended. If email exposure is unwanted, rewrite author/committer metadata before publication using the owner’s chosen public/noreply identity.

findings.evidence: One /home-style path occurs inside a publicly copied self-driving tutorial; the other three apparent home paths are normal GTEx/ArcGIS URL paths. Fourteen RFC1918 IP matches belong to described cybersecurity lab/emulation networks, duplicated in cache JSON/CSV. None identified the owner’s workstation, internal server or study infrastructure.
findings.fix: No privacy-driven redaction of study metadata is required for these false positives; the archive-removal recommendation independently removes this irrelevant material.

findings.evidence: All five local sample assets visually contain eye images/figure panels without visible patient names, faces or text identifiers. No PNG text/EXIF metadata in gallery PNGs and no JPEG XMP found. OCTDL has an EXIF IFD containing only orientation tag 0x0112; no name, date, GPS or author field found. Filename/subject/laterality identifiers are provenance/pseudonymous keys rather than demonstrated real-person identity. Existing public sample labels alone are not a new clinical spreadsheet.
findings.fix: Retain hashes and attribution; no image transformation or privacy redaction indicated by this inspection. Do not extrapolate this result to the source datasets.

findings.evidence: All 479 cards have nonempty Overview and Examples and previews sections; official_url and access_url are populated for all 479. Twenty-eight extension records have frozen description=Unknown, but their current reviewed overview is present. Cards without local examples explicitly state availability is Unknown and link an official source. The English example/source-entry promise is supported as a link promise, not a guarantee of downloadable image previews. The 244 excluded names were screened; disease, childhood and ethnicity terms are ordinary public scientific descriptions, not grounds for suppression and not patient identities.
findings.fix: No blocking wording defect found. Keep the existing Unknown/local-example limitations and avoid upgrading official source links into verified image-preview claims.

findings.evidence: Non-archive email matches are academic authors, upstream project attribution and official study/application contacts, repeated in CSV/SQLite/HTML outputs. The archive has additional author/contact and commercial-cache addresses. These were not classified as patient emails or owner credentials.
findings.fix: Retain source-backed academic/contact details where necessary; avoid republishing unrelated commercial-cache contacts by removing the archive.

negative_checks.archive_inline_data_image_result: One data:image base64 occurrence is a code-format placeholder {mask_base64}, not embedded image bytes; 118 descriptions include remote image markup, which is not local media payload.

limits: No credential-validation attempts, account access, actual image downloads or visibility changes were performed.
Pattern-based secret and identifier scans plus contextual review do not prove absence of arbitrary unknown-format secrets or all possible privacy risk.
A source being public does not itself resolve third-party licensing or patient consent; no legal conclusion is asserted.
The audit covers the named commit and identical tracked worktree at time of inspection, not future edits.
Initial known-token regex counters do not include the separately reviewed opaque share/CASA/extraction-code findings; zero pattern hits must not be interpreted as zero access-bearing strings.
